subject: RE: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, SSO, KMS)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@acme-corp.com>; Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, SSO, KMS)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the context on your evaluation criteria and the timeline (POC by end of February). Attached is a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the milestones we discussed and ownership on both sides. High-level POC milestone: "POC environment setup" — the items we need to unblock that are listed below.

Quick summary of the POC env dependencies (we included these in the attached MAP and network sheet):
- VPC peering / Private connectivity: Acme to Redwood VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway.
- IP allowlists: Static IPs for egress (we can provide the ranges once you confirm the VPC approach).
- SSO / SAML: Connect Acme IdP (Okta) to Redwood Console for admin access and test users for the POC.
- Secrets / KMS: Customer-managed KMS key for any secrets at rest and access policies for the POC.

Proposed next steps / asks from Acme for the POC milestone:
1) Confirm whether you prefer VPC peering or a public IP allowlist flow (we can support both for the POC).
2) Provide a primary network contact and SSO admin for Okta configuration.
3) Approve the MAP milestones and target close date (we put a provisional POC start date of 2026-02-08 and target POC complete 2026-02-26).

I'll loop in Rishi (AM) and Lukas (SE) to align on the implementation tasks once you confirm the network approach. If it's helpful, we can schedule a 30-min network/infra wash with your cloud networking team this week.

Thanks — I attached the MAP draft and the network requirements workbook for your team to review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_AcmeCorp.pdf, network_requirements_acme.xlsx

Marissa —

Thanks for the notes and the MAP. Quick answers from our side:
- We prefer VPC peering for secure connectivity (we want private traffic for the POC).
- Primary network contact: Tom Nguyen (cc'd).
- SSO: We use Okta; our SSO admin is me (I can create a temporary test group if needed).
- KMS: We will use our customer-managed KMS key — I will share the key ARN after I confirm with InfoSec.

A few clarifying Qs:
1) For VPC peering, do you need any specific route table changes or will Redwood provide a peering guide?
2) For static egress IPs: do you have a minimum list to start with so our firewall team can pre-approve?
3) If we hit a blocker on peering, can we fall back to IP allowlist for the POC only?

We can commit to the 2026-02-08 start window assuming the network items are straightforward. Happy to do a 30-min call with Lukas and Tom this week — Tom, are you available Wed 14th at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. Product Security Manager | Acme Corp
sarah.patel@acme-corp.com

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@acme-corp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP draft & POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, SSO, KMS)

Hi all —

Thanks — quick technical notes / checklist to include in the MAP under the POC environment milestone. I'll join the Wed 14th network wash if scheduled, otherwise we can do a separate call.

POC environment: Redwood <> Acme networking checklist (POC)
- VPC peering: We support AWS-to-AWS peering in the same region. Requirements:
  - Acme to provide VPC ID and CIDR block (no overlap with Redwood VPC 10.40.0.0/16).
  - Update Acme route tables to point relevant subnets to the peering connection.
  - Security groups: allow inbound on TCP 443 from Redwood peered CIDR for control plane endpoints.
- IP allowlist fallback: if peering is delayed, allow these egress ranges for POC: 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24 (we'll confirm exact prefixes in prod).
- SSO / SAML: We support Okta with metadata URL or SAML metadata file. Need: SSO admin to create a test group and provide either metadata URL or an exported XML, plus a test user. We'll configure SP-initiated SSO for the POC.
- KMS / Secrets: For the POC using customer-managed KMS, we need the KMS key ARN and a short IAM policy allowing decrypt for the POC service principal (we can provide the policy snippet). For secrets, we'll accept a vaulted secret or reference to your KMS-wrapped secret.

Timing / capacity notes (Rishi):
- POC start 2026-02-08 is feasible. Recommend we reserve 2 dedicated vCPU-equivalent nodes for the 3-week window for predictable latency; Rishi: can you confirm availability and any cost implications?

Next concrete items for Acme to action:
1) Share VPC ID + CIDR 
2) Share Okta metadata URL or SAML XML + create test user/group
3) Share KMS key ARN or confirm if you want Redwood-managed keys for the POC

I'll draft a short implementation checklist and drop it into the shared Drive folder. Once we have the items above, we can provision the POC environment in ~3 business days.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood-inference.com
